=== ENTITIES ===

[ZODIAC]
Description: "ZODIAC" refers to the notorious and unidentified serial killer whose identity, crimes, letters, and patterns are the central focus of extensive investigations. This "very bad man" and criminal is responsible for a series of unsolved murders, including a believed 1966 Southern California murder. The killer adopted the moniker "Zodiac" and is associated with a distinctive crosshair symbol.

The Zodiac Killer communicated through calls and letters, with handwriting from these letters being a key piece of evidence. The activities, claims, and potential true identity of Zodiac have been the subject of ongoing police and journalistic investigations, notably by Sergeant Bawart and Detective Toschi in the past.

Robert Graysmith became obsessed with the case, investigating it extensively and eventually writing a book titled "Zodiac," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. Graysmith even sketched a costume for Zodiac, inspired by Count Zaroff.

Arthur Leigh Allen is a prominent suspect in the case, having allegedly planned to use the name "Zodiac" to communicate with the police. He was also noted to have worn the Zodiac crosshair symbol on his watch and mentioned the name a year and a half before it appeared in any of the killer's letters. Another individual, Sam, is implied to be the Zodiac caller. Despite these leads and suspects, the true identity of the Zodiac Killer remains unknown.

[TAXI DRIVER MURDER]
Description: The murder of a taxi driver, for which the Zodiac killer claims responsibility, occurring near Washington Street and Maple Street.

[SAN FRANCISCO CHRONICLE]
Description: The SAN FRANCISCO CHRONICLE is a major, grand old newspaper building located on Fifth and Mission in San Francisco, often referred to informally as "the Chron" or "the Chronicle."

The newspaper serves as a workplace for a significant number of reporters, columnists, and staff members, many of whom are central to the investigation of the Zodiac killer. Notable employees include Paul Avery, a reporter and columnist who extensively covers the Zodiac case, attempts to influence the investigation, and monitors related broadcasts; Robert Graysmith, a cartoonist and reporter who works on the third floor, investigates the Zodiac killings, and uses the newspaper as a base for his inquiries; Duffy Jennings, who now works there; columnists Herb Caen and Armistead Maupin; and other staff members such as Shorty, Carol Fisher, Templeton Peck, Charles De Young Theriot, and Hyman. Detectives Toschi and Armstrong are also noted to visit the newspaper office.

The SAN FRANCISCO CHRONICLE plays a pivotal role in the Zodiac killer case, as it is the primary recipient of letters, ciphers, and coded messages from the killer, including those claiming responsibility for murders. The newspaper faces critical decisions regarding whether to publish these communications, often engaging in internal debates about their content and potential impact. It cooperates with the San Francisco Police Department (SFPD) on publishing Zodiac letters and has published various articles related to the killer, including a front-page story about a police officer shooting. Its journalists actively investigate the Zodiac killings, using the newspaper office as a hub for their efforts and monitoring live television broadcasts related to the case.

[OCTOBER 14, 1969]
Description: The date the Zodiac killer's letter, claiming responsibility for murders, arrived at the San Francisco Chronicle.

[NEW LETTER]
Description: A communication sent by the Zodiac killer to the San Francisco Chronicle, where he identifies himself as "The Zodiac" and provides further details about his crimes.

=== ENTITIES ===

[DAVE TOSCHI]
Description: Dave Toschi is an Italian-American Inspector and detective, described as handsome. He was involved in an investigation, being called to a crime scene and working alongside Armstrong and Captain Lee to obtain a warrant for Arthur Leigh Allen. Later, Toschi provided advice to Mulanax, recommending against sharing files with Graysmith, and agreed that the investigation into the suspect (Lee/Leigh) was considered over.

[BILL ARMSTRONG]
Description: Bill Armstrong is portrayed as a dedicated law enforcement officer, holding roles as a plain clothes cop, an Inspector, and a detective, and is noted for his silver hair. He has a significant professional relationship with Inspector Dave Toschi, having been his former partner and continuing to collaborate closely with him, as well as with Captain Lee, on various investigations. Armstrong was deeply involved in the Zodiac murders investigation; he previously investigated claims related to the Zodiac Killer's birthday, though he found no matches among suspects. Later, he played a crucial role in the investigation of Arthur Leigh Allen, leading Allen's interrogation and presenting evidence to secure a warrant against him. Armstrong also contacted Toschi regarding a shooting incident and met him at the crime scene, underscoring his active participation in police work.

[TOSCHI]
Description: **TOSCHI** is a prominent and deeply invested detective and inspector, primarily affiliated with the Homicide Unit of the San Francisco Police Department (SFPD) at the Hall of Justice. He is widely recognized as the lead investigator in the complex and frustrating Zodiac Killer case.

Throughout his extensive involvement, Toschi worked closely with partners such as Armstrong, Mulanax, Narlow, and Nicolai, and briefed superiors like Captain Lee and Captain Cross. He was instrumental in leading the police investigation, actively pursuing leads, and coordinating with various law enforcement personnel. His duties included leading the search of Arthur Leigh Allen's residence, interviewing suspects like Allen, and reviewing evidence, including Robert Graysmith's findings linking Allen to the Zodiac.

Toschi received direct communications from the Zodiac Killer and even a letter from Leigh Allen. He was closely involved with the Office of Questioned Documents, consulting with experts like Terry Pascoe on handwriting analysis, though he often expressed impatience with the pace of their work. He regularly visited the scene of Paul Stine's murder at Washington and Cherry, sitting vigil and interviewing patrolmen Fouke and Zelms.

His dedication to the case was evident in his frustration with the lack of progress, the public's fear, and the press. He led meetings with bus drivers, monitored television broadcasts, and coordinated responses to the Zodiac's calls. Toschi was also the focus of Melvin Belli's attention during a broadcast and escorted Belli to KGO Television. He was mentioned in a Zodiac letter himself, leading to an approach by Internal Affairs for a handwriting sample.

Toschi was a key consultant for Robert Graysmith, initially reluctant but eventually providing crucial leads and advice. He discussed theories and evidence with Graysmith, expressing his strong belief that Arthur Leigh Allen was the killer. Graysmith often echoed Toschi's observations and even woke him in the middle of the night with new discoveries. Toschi also investigated the Cheri Jo Bates murder for its potential Zodiac connection and examined Zodiac letters and bomb diagrams, suggesting military consultation.

Despite the immense pressure and the case's toll, Toschi remained deeply committed, though at one point he was implied to be trying to distance himself from the case, perhaps due to burnout or its unresolved nature. He is an experienced murder police officer whose work on the Zodiac case made him a central figure in the investigation.

[DAVE]

=== ENTITIES ===

[PAUL STINE]
Description: Paul Stine was a single male cab driver who was murdered by the Zodiac Killer at Washington and Cherry, where he was pronounced dead at the scene. His murder was considered a significant deviation from the Zodiac Killer's typical pattern of attacks, as it did not fit the mold of previous incidents. As a victim of the Zodiac Killer, a piece of Paul Stine's bloody shirt was sent to Avery. His case is a crucial part of Inspector Toschi's investigation and is also a subject of discussion between Graysmith and Toschi.

[ZODIAC]
Description: "ZODIAC" refers to the notorious and unidentified serial killer whose identity, crimes, letters, and patterns are the central focus of extensive investigations. This "very bad man" and criminal is responsible for a series of unsolved murders, including a believed 1966 Southern California murder. The killer adopted the moniker "Zodiac" and is associated with a distinctive crosshair symbol.

The Zodiac Killer communicated through calls and letters, with handwriting from these letters being a key piece of evidence. The activities, claims, and potential true identity of Zodiac have been the subject of ongoing police and journalistic investigations, notably by Sergeant Bawart and Detective Toschi in the past.

Robert Graysmith became obsessed with the case, investigating it extensively and eventually writing a book titled "Zodiac," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. Graysmith even sketched a costume for Zodiac, inspired by Count Zaroff.

Arthur Leigh Allen is a prominent suspect in the case, having allegedly planned to use the name "Zodiac" to communicate with the police. He was also noted to have worn the Zodiac crosshair symbol on his watch and mentioned the name a year and a half before it appeared in any of the killer's letters. Another individual, Sam, is implied to be the Zodiac caller. Despite these leads and suspects, the true identity of the Zodiac Killer remains unknown.

[RECENT ATTACKS]
Description: A series of attacks that led police to order curfews in several counties in the San Francisco Bay Area

[MURDERS]
Description: No description available

[ZODIAC KILLER]
Description: The ZODIAC KILLER was a real-life serial killer active in California during the late 1960s and early 1970s. This individual was responsible for multiple murders and sent numerous letters, some of which included swatches of victim Paul Stine's shirt. The Zodiac Killer claimed responsibility for Paul Stine's murder and also issued threats, including one to "wipe out a school bus." The killer's distinctive letter style has been noted. The attacks and symbols associated with the Zodiac Killer have been the subject of extensive investigation, notably by Robert Graysmith, and the killer's timeline has been compared to that of Arthur Leigh Allen.

[ZODIAC ATTACKS]
Description: No description available

question: What does the police discover while interviewing Allen?
response: While interviewing Arthur Leigh Allen, the police discover that he claims to have been in Southern California around the same time as the Riverside killing, and that he was a Navy man who wears size 10 1/2 boots, the same size found at Berryessa. They also learn that he was fired from Valley Springs for touching his students, and that he is not ambidextrous, despite claims to the contrary. Additionally, they discover he owns a watch with the Zodiac symbol and the word "Zodiac" on it, which he received as a Christmas gift two years prior. [Data: ARTHUR LEIGH ALLEN]

[ARTHUR LEIGH ALLEN]
Description: Arthur Leigh Allen, born December 18, 1933, was the primary suspect in the Zodiac Killer case, identified by Graysmith as the perpetrator in his investigation and by "Mike" as his shooter. He was widely believed to be the "Zodiac" killer.

Allen had a background as a Navy man and worked as a chemist, including at Union Oil in Pinole. He was also a former public school teacher, specifically at Valley Springs, but was fired from elementary schools for molesting children or touching kids. Notably, he was fired eight months before the first Vallejo murder. He was later arrested for molestation in January 1975.

Regarding his connection to the Zodiac case, Allen was interrogated by Inspectors Armstrong, Toschi, and Sergeant Mulanax, and his investigation was reopened by Sergeant Bawart. He denied involvement in the murders and provided explanations for incriminating statements and items. He was interviewed by Toschi on August 4, 1971, and also wrote a letter to Toschi. Allegations against him included discussing hunting people and using the name "Zodiac" in 1968.

Investigators conducted searches of his residence and basement (in 1991), and he was brought to the Hall of Justice for investigation. He was known to drive a white Kharmann Ghia. While he was noted to live in Vallejo at some point, his trailer was moved to Santa Rosa on August 7, 1971, indicating a later residence there.

Allen was described as being sick with diabetes and possibly ambidextrous. He died of a heart attack in 1992 before he could be arrested for the murders. DNA tests conducted on Zodiac envelopes did not match his DNA.

=== ENTITIES ===

[ARTHUR LEIGH ALLEN]
Description: Arthur Leigh Allen, born December 18, 1933, was the primary suspect in the Zodiac Killer case, identified by Graysmith as the perpetrator in his investigation and by "Mike" as his shooter. He was widely believed to be the "Zodiac" killer.

Allen had a background as a Navy man and worked as a chemist, including at Union Oil in Pinole. He was also a former public school teacher, specifically at Valley Springs, but was fired from elementary schools for molesting children or touching kids. Notably, he was fired eight months before the first Vallejo murder. He was later arrested for molestation in January 1975.

Regarding his connection to the Zodiac case, Allen was interrogated by Inspectors Armstrong, Toschi, and Sergeant Mulanax, and his investigation was reopened by Sergeant Bawart. He denied involvement in the murders and provided explanations for incriminating statements and items. He was interviewed by Toschi on August 4, 1971, and also wrote a letter to Toschi. Allegations against him included discussing hunting people and using the name "Zodiac" in 1968.

Investigators conducted searches of his residence and basement (in 1991), and he was brought to the Hall of Justice for investigation. He was known to drive a white Kharmann Ghia. While he was noted to live in Vallejo at some point, his trailer was moved to Santa Rosa on August 7, 1971, indicating a later residence there.

Allen was described as being sick with diabetes and possibly ambidextrous. He died of a heart attack in 1992 before he could be arrested for the murders. DNA tests conducted on Zodiac envelopes did not match his DNA.

[SHERWOOD]
Description: Sherwood is a central figure in the Zodiac investigation, primarily recognized as a handwriting expert and forensic specialist. He served as the head of the "Questioned Documents" department, a role that entailed receiving and analyzing various pieces of evidence, including letters pertinent to the case. Sherwood was also responsible for training Terry Pascoe in handwriting analysis.

During the course of the investigation, Sherwood obtained and analyzed handwriting samples. His initial assessment of Arthur Leigh Allen's handwriting samples did not yield a match, leading him to disqualify Allen as a suspect. This decision resulted in him ruling out a suspect that Inspector Toschi had mentioned. However, Toschi later suggested that Sherwood should "try again," indicating a potential desire for further review or a differing opinion on the findings.

At a later stage, Sherwood, by then a former employee of the "Questioned Documents" department, provided assistance to Graysmith with handwriting samples related to the Zodiac case. He was also mentioned by Paul Avery, who suggested that Toschi should address Sherwood regarding the case, possibly in his capacity as a forensic authority or a superior within the investigative framework. Graysmith also made a personal observation, suggesting that Sherwood drinks heavily.

[MORRILL]
Description: MORRILL is a handwriting analyst and expert who works within the Questioned Documents unit. He was significantly involved in the Zodiac investigation, providing crucial forensic analysis. MORRILL assisted Graysmith by examining handwriting samples, including those related to Rick Marshall, and analyzing the Zodiac's letters. A key contribution was his analysis of Arthur Leigh Allen's handwriting exemplars, from which he concluded that Allen's writing did not match that of the Zodiac killer. Furthermore, MORRILL noted changes in watermark paper and handwriting analysis pertinent to the case. His office was mentioned in the context of the police investigation, and he also received a visit from Wallace Penny.

[ALLEN]
Description: A primary suspect in the Zodiac killer investigation, whose handwriting is being analyzed and for whom police are attempting to obtain a search warrant.

[QUESTIONED DOCUMENTS]
Description: "QUESTIONED DOCUMENTS" is identified as a department, unit, or specialized unit, likely operating within a law enforcement or forensic agency. Its core responsibility is the analysis of handwriting and other document-related evidence. The department is staffed by experts, including handwriting expert Terry Pascoe, who was consulted by Toschi, and Morrill, who is also employed there. Sherwood was associated with "QUESTIONED DOCUMENTS," having headed the department for handwriting analysis specifically in the Zodiac case, though he was subsequently fired from the unit. In the context of the Zodiac letters, the experts within "QUESTIONED DOCUMENTS" provided inconclusive results.

=== ENTITIES ===

[ZODIAC]
Description: "ZODIAC" refers to the notorious and unidentified serial killer whose identity, crimes, letters, and patterns are the central focus of extensive investigations. This "very bad man" and criminal is responsible for a series of unsolved murders, including a believed 1966 Southern California murder. The killer adopted the moniker "Zodiac" and is associated with a distinctive crosshair symbol.

The Zodiac Killer communicated through calls and letters, with handwriting from these letters being a key piece of evidence. The activities, claims, and potential true identity of Zodiac have been the subject of ongoing police and journalistic investigations, notably by Sergeant Bawart and Detective Toschi in the past.

Robert Graysmith became obsessed with the case, investigating it extensively and eventually writing a book titled "Zodiac," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. Graysmith even sketched a costume for Zodiac, inspired by Count Zaroff.

Arthur Leigh Allen is a prominent suspect in the case, having allegedly planned to use the name "Zodiac" to communicate with the police. He was also noted to have worn the Zodiac crosshair symbol on his watch and mentioned the name a year and a half before it appeared in any of the killer's letters. Another individual, Sam, is implied to be the Zodiac caller. Despite these leads and suspects, the true identity of the Zodiac Killer remains unknown.

[ARTHUR LEIGH ALLEN]
Description: Arthur Leigh Allen, born December 18, 1933, was the primary suspect in the Zodiac Killer case, identified by Graysmith as the perpetrator in his investigation and by "Mike" as his shooter. He was widely believed to be the "Zodiac" killer.

Allen had a background as a Navy man and worked as a chemist, including at Union Oil in Pinole. He was also a former public school teacher, specifically at Valley Springs, but was fired from elementary schools for molesting children or touching kids. Notably, he was fired eight months before the first Vallejo murder. He was later arrested for molestation in January 1975.

Regarding his connection to the Zodiac case, Allen was interrogated by Inspectors Armstrong, Toschi, and Sergeant Mulanax, and his investigation was reopened by Sergeant Bawart. He denied involvement in the murders and provided explanations for incriminating statements and items. He was interviewed by Toschi on August 4, 1971, and also wrote a letter to Toschi. Allegations against him included discussing hunting people and using the name "Zodiac" in 1968.

Investigators conducted searches of his residence and basement (in 1991), and he was brought to the Hall of Justice for investigation. He was known to drive a white Kharmann Ghia. While he was noted to live in Vallejo at some point, his trailer was moved to Santa Rosa on August 7, 1971, indicating a later residence there.

Allen was described as being sick with diabetes and possibly ambidextrous. He died of a heart attack in 1992 before he could be arrested for the murders. DNA tests conducted on Zodiac envelopes did not match his DNA.

[ARTHUR LEIGH ALLEN'S DEATH]
Description: No description available

[SUNSET TRAILER COURT]
Description: The current residence of Arthur Leigh Allen, located in Santa Rosa, California, which is searched by police.

=== ENTITIES ===

[ROBERT GRAYSMITH]
Description: Robert Graysmith was a cartoonist at the San Francisco Chronicle who developed a profound interest in the Zodiac killer's codes and letters, dedicating himself to deciphering them. Living in San Francisco, he was in his mid-20s, a father to David, and Melanie's partner, residing in a cluttered apartment. He reacted negatively to news about a rapist and later stopped receiving anonymous phone calls after Arthur Leigh Allen's death.

Graysmith's deep fascination with the Zodiac case led him to collect newspaper clippings and conduct extensive personal research into the killer's codes. He expressed his interest in the case to Dave Toschi and visited Paul Avery to discuss the possibility of writing a book about it. He also met with Vaughn to discuss a film and a film canister pertinent to his investigation.

His dedicated work as a civilian investigator culminated in him authoring the books "Zodiac" and "Zodiac Unmasked," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. His investigations and writings were instrumental in leading to the reopening of the Zodiac case, with a focus on Arthur Leigh Allen. Despite his significant contributions to the case, his conclusions on the Zodiac case are believed by many to be incorrect.

[ZODIAC UNMASKED]
Description: A book written by Robert Graysmith, which the script "Chronicles" is based on.

[BOOKS]
Description: BOOKS are described as materials and objects of research. They were utilized by David and Aaron for their Zodiac investigation. Additionally, BOOKS served as objects of research for Robert Graysmith, with some of these materials notably having been stolen from libraries.

[GRAYSMITH]
Description: Robert Graysmith is a cartoonist at the San Francisco Chronicle who becomes deeply and intensely involved in the investigation of the Zodiac killer, often to the detriment of his personal life. Initially observing discussions about the murderer's letters and ciphers, he quickly develops an obsession with the case. Graysmith meticulously studies codebreaking, recreates ciphers from memory, and successfully decodes one of the Zodiac's ciphers, cross-referencing lunar cycles with the killer's timeline.

He is a diligent investigator, collecting and reading Zodiac letters and newspaper articles, focusing on patterns in the killer's communications and activities, such as the "Zodiac Riverside Connection." Graysmith observes deviations in the killer's patterns, like in Paul Stine's murder, and uses library books and resources like "Homicide Investigations" by Lemoyne Snyder to develop theories, including a "water theory."

Graysmith collaborates with and consults numerous individuals, including his colleague Paul Avery at the Chronicle, Inspector David Toschi, Mel Nicolai, Narlow, and handwriting expert Morrill. He seeks information from police departments in Napa and Vallejo, visits key locations like Vaughn's basement and Linda Del Buono at San Joaquin County Honor Camp, and pursues leads such as seeking Rick Marshall's handwriting samples. He eventually compiles extensive "Zodiac Files" and authors a book about the case.

In his personal life, Graysmith is a father to Margot, David, and Aaron, and is married to Melanie. He is shown listening to radio programs with his son David and expresses concern for his son's safety due to the Zodiac's threats. His relentless pursuit of the truth leads him to present evidence linking Arthur Leigh Allen to the Zodiac, theorize about Allen's connection to the crimes, and eventually confront him, remaining persistent despite exhaustion.

[ZODIAC ALPHABET]
Description: A cipher found in a medieval-themed book, which Graysmith discovered had many symbols identical to the First Code used by the Zodiac."

question: Why does Graysmith's wife leave him?
response: Graysmith's wife, Melanie, leaves him because she is scared by his obsessive investigation into the Zodiac killer. She fears for his safety and the negative impact his all-consuming research is having on their family, including his neglect of family duties. Melanie is also worried about the publicity of his research, knowing the killer reads newspapers.

=== ENTITIES ===

[SOCCER]
Description: Soccer is an activity Graysmith's sons participate in, from which Graysmith was supposed to pick them up.

[MR. BELLI]
Description: A person whose movements (leaving on the 18th and returning on Christmas) are being discussed by Graysmith and the Housekeeper.

[MARGOT]
Description: Margot is Graysmith's 2-year-old daughter. She is described as a baby or young child who accompanies Graysmith, including in his car. Graysmith is observed feeding Margot from a bottle.

[MELANIE]
Description: Melanie is Robert Graysmith's wife and partner, with whom he lives and shares children, including a daughter. She is deeply concerned about Graysmith's obsessive investigation into the Zodiac Killer, fearing for his safety and the potential danger it poses to their family. Melanie is scared by his obsession and worried about its impact on their children, as well as his neglect of family duties. Her concerns extend to the publicity of his research in newspapers, knowing the killer's habit of reading them, and she also expresses concern for Paul Avery's safety.

Melanie is frequently present in Graysmith's home, including his bedroom, and comments on his extensive collection of Zodiac-related materials. She reacts with fear to a mysterious phone call Graysmith receives. She has been seen having dinner with Graysmith, providing him with change for a phone call, and accompanying him to a movie screening. On one occasion, while waiting for news with Graysmith at his home, she described their situation as an "interesting date." Melanie also works for Glynnis.

[GRAYSMITH]
Description: Robert Graysmith is a cartoonist at the San Francisco Chronicle who becomes deeply and intensely involved in the investigation of the Zodiac killer, often to the detriment of his personal life. Initially observing discussions about the murderer's letters and ciphers, he quickly develops an obsession with the case. Graysmith meticulously studies codebreaking, recreates ciphers from memory, and successfully decodes one of the Zodiac's ciphers, cross-referencing lunar cycles with the killer's timeline.

He is a diligent investigator, collecting and reading Zodiac letters and newspaper articles, focusing on patterns in the killer's communications and activities, such as the "Zodiac Riverside Connection." Graysmith observes deviations in the killer's patterns, like in Paul Stine's murder, and uses library books and resources like "Homicide Investigations" by Lemoyne Snyder to develop theories, including a "water theory."

Graysmith collaborates with and consults numerous individuals, including his colleague Paul Avery at the Chronicle, Inspector David Toschi, Mel Nicolai, Narlow, and handwriting expert Morrill. He seeks information from police departments in Napa and Vallejo, visits key locations like Vaughn's basement and Linda Del Buono at San Joaquin County Honor Camp, and pursues leads such as seeking Rick Marshall's handwriting samples. He eventually compiles extensive "Zodiac Files" and authors a book about the case.

In his personal life, Graysmith is a father to Margot, David, and Aaron, and is married to Melanie. He is shown listening to radio programs with his son David and expresses concern for his son's safety due to the Zodiac's threats. His relentless pursuit of the truth leads him to present evidence linking Arthur Leigh Allen to the Zodiac, theorize about Allen's connection to the crimes, and eventually confront him, remaining persistent despite exhaustion.

=== ENTITIES ===

[LEIGH ALLEN]
Description: Leigh Allen is identified as a primary suspect in the Zodiac killer case. He was interviewed by detectives, who also sought to search his trailer for evidence. Allen lived in a trailer and attended school in Santa Rosa. He is noted as the brother of John Allen and the brother-in-law of Catherine Allen. Further details about his life include that he lived near Darlene Ferrin and worked at Ace Hardware. At one point, Leigh Allen was incarcerated at Atascadero and was confronted by Graysmith.

[ACE HARDWARE]
Description: The store where Leigh Allen worked and was confronted by Graysmith.

[ZODIAC]
Description: "ZODIAC" refers to the notorious and unidentified serial killer whose identity, crimes, letters, and patterns are the central focus of extensive investigations. This "very bad man" and criminal is responsible for a series of unsolved murders, including a believed 1966 Southern California murder. The killer adopted the moniker "Zodiac" and is associated with a distinctive crosshair symbol.

The Zodiac Killer communicated through calls and letters, with handwriting from these letters being a key piece of evidence. The activities, claims, and potential true identity of Zodiac have been the subject of ongoing police and journalistic investigations, notably by Sergeant Bawart and Detective Toschi in the past.

Robert Graysmith became obsessed with the case, investigating it extensively and eventually writing a book titled "Zodiac," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. Graysmith even sketched a costume for Zodiac, inspired by Count Zaroff.

Arthur Leigh Allen is a prominent suspect in the case, having allegedly planned to use the name "Zodiac" to communicate with the police. He was also noted to have worn the Zodiac crosshair symbol on his watch and mentioned the name a year and a half before it appeared in any of the killer's letters. Another individual, Sam, is implied to be the Zodiac caller. Despite these leads and suspects, the true identity of the Zodiac Killer remains unknown.

[ROBERT GRAYSMITH]
Description: Robert Graysmith was a cartoonist at the San Francisco Chronicle who developed a profound interest in the Zodiac killer's codes and letters, dedicating himself to deciphering them. Living in San Francisco, he was in his mid-20s, a father to David, and Melanie's partner, residing in a cluttered apartment. He reacted negatively to news about a rapist and later stopped receiving anonymous phone calls after Arthur Leigh Allen's death.

Graysmith's deep fascination with the Zodiac case led him to collect newspaper clippings and conduct extensive personal research into the killer's codes. He expressed his interest in the case to Dave Toschi and visited Paul Avery to discuss the possibility of writing a book about it. He also met with Vaughn to discuss a film and a film canister pertinent to his investigation.

His dedicated work as a civilian investigator culminated in him authoring the books "Zodiac" and "Zodiac Unmasked," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. His investigations and writings were instrumental in leading to the reopening of the Zodiac case, with a focus on Arthur Leigh Allen. Despite his significant contributions to the case, his conclusions on the Zodiac case are believed by many to be incorrect.

[LINDA]
Description: Linda is a woman whom Graysmith locates in the San Joaquin County Honor Camp. He is actively trying to track her down and find her for information related to his investigation into the Zodiac case, believing she is "the key" to identifying Marshall. Graysmith questions Linda about Darlene and a "painting party," as Linda knew Darlene and remembers details about a "weird" guy who brought presents from Mexico and claimed to have killed someone. Furthermore, a statement from Linda, found in the Vallejo files, suggests that Arthur Leigh Allen knew her.

[GRAYSMITH]
Description: Robert Graysmith is a cartoonist at the San Francisco Chronicle who becomes deeply and intensely involved in the investigation of the Zodiac killer, often to the detriment of his personal life. Initially observing discussions about the murderer's letters and ciphers, he quickly develops an obsession with the case. Graysmith meticulously studies codebreaking, recreates ciphers from memory, and successfully decodes one of the Zodiac's ciphers, cross-referencing lunar cycles with the killer's timeline.

He is a diligent investigator, collecting and reading Zodiac letters and newspaper articles, focusing on patterns in the killer's communications and activities, such as the "Zodiac Riverside Connection." Graysmith observes deviations in the killer's patterns, like in Paul Stine's murder, and uses library books and resources like "Homicide Investigations" by Lemoyne Snyder to develop theories, including a "water theory."

Graysmith collaborates with and consults numerous individuals, including his colleague Paul Avery at the Chronicle, Inspector David Toschi, Mel Nicolai, Narlow, and handwriting expert Morrill. He seeks information from police departments in Napa and Vallejo, visits key locations like Vaughn's basement and Linda Del Buono at San Joaquin County Honor Camp, and pursues leads such as seeking Rick Marshall's handwriting samples. He eventually compiles extensive "Zodiac Files" and authors a book about the case.

In his personal life, Graysmith is a father to Margot, David, and Aaron, and is married to Melanie. He is shown listening to radio programs with his son David and expresses concern for his son's safety due to the Zodiac's threats. His relentless pursuit of the truth leads him to present evidence linking Arthur Leigh Allen to the Zodiac, theorize about Allen's connection to the crimes, and eventually confront him, remaining persistent despite exhaustion.

[SACRAMENTO BEE]
Description: A newspaper organization where Paul Avery now works after leaving the San Francisco Chronicle. It is referred to as "the Bee" in the text.

[PAUL AVERY]
Description: Paul Avery is a journalist, described as a "great reporter" and a well-dressed crime reporter. He initially worked on the third floor of the San Francisco Chronicle, where he was a colleague of Robert Graysmith. During his tenure at the Chronicle, Avery wrote numerous articles about the Zodiac case, provided information, and discussed the killer's activities and messages with Graysmith. He was directly threatened by the Zodiac killer and attempted to interview Inspector Toschi, whom Graysmith believed Avery might know.

Later in his career, Paul Avery moved to the Sacramento Bee, where he lived on a houseboat. By this point, his perspective on the Zodiac case had shifted; he became dismissive of its importance, focusing instead on selling newspapers, and reacted with cynicism to news of Graysmith's success in decoding the Zodiac's cipher. Despite this change, Graysmith still sought him out to discuss writing a book about Zodiac. Avery was also known to follow leads, such as one in Riverside to meet an anonymous tipster, for which he carried a gun. His drinking habits were significant enough to be used by Graysmith as a comparison for another individual.

[CHRONICLE]
Description: The CHRONICLE, specifically identified as The San Francisco Chronicle, is a prominent big city newspaper and media organization. It serves as the workplace for reporter Paul Avery, who covers news related to the case, and also for Robert Graysmith. The newspaper is known for publishing news about the case, including the Zodiac killer's letters. Due to its decision to print these letters, The San Francisco Chronicle was accused by a radio caller of encouraging the Zodiac killer.

[AVERY]
Description: Paul Avery is a prominent crime reporter and journalist for the San Francisco Chronicle, deeply involved in the investigation of the Zodiac killer. He is also known as a Zodiac target, having received a threatening letter and a piece of a victim's shirt directly from the killer, making him a direct recipient of the Zodiac's threats. Avery diligently investigates the case, uncovering new information and taking evidence to the Office of Questioned Documents. He covers crime in Vallejo, verifies murder details with the police, and confirms details of the shootings.

As a key figure at the Chronicle, Avery is actively engaged in the newsroom's response to the Zodiac. He files and types notes about potential Zodiac calls, writes articles about the killer, and is present for discussions about new Zodiac letters, even reading one aloud to colleagues and detectives. He also takes diligent notes on the Zodiac killer's statements during live broadcasts and is involved in debates about publishing the letters, sometimes revealing information about police requests to hold off on publication. Despite his deep involvement, his behavior can be erratic, leading to conflicts with his superior, Peck. He is also found asleep in his car on one occasion.

Avery frequently interacts with Graysmith regarding the Zodiac case. While sometimes questioning Graysmith's motives and findings, he also works with him, providing insights into the Zodiac's methods, motivations, and the origin of his symbol. Their discussions cover various aspects of the case, including Paul Stine's murder, Toschi's gun style, Kathleen Johns, and even Graysmith's "water theory," which Avery dismisses. He meets with Graysmith at Morti's to discuss codes and investigation methods, and receives exemplars from Captain Cross. Avery also discusses "The Most Dangerous Game" and Count Zaroff, indicating a broader intellectual engagement. He is seen discussing the Zodiac case with Graysmith and Hyman, and watches broadcasts with other reporters at the San Francisco Chronicle.

=== ENTITIES ===

[DARLENE FERRIN]
Description: Darlene Ferrin was a 22-year-old woman who tragically became a victim of the Zodiac killer. On July 4th, she was driving and picked up Mike Mageau, shortly before she was shot and murdered at Blue Rock Springs. She did not survive the attack. Her case is a significant part of the Vallejo investigation into the Zodiac killer, and her murder and connections are also being investigated by Graysmith and Toschi. Florence Douglas mentioned Darlene Ferrin's case, suggesting that crucial clues might have been overlooked. Darlene Ferrin reportedly knew a man named "Lee," who is suspected to be Leigh Allen. Prior to her death, she was reportedly scared of an unknown man she had encountered at a painting party, and she was followed before the fatal shooting.

[MIKE MAGEAU]
Description: Mike Mageau was a 19-year-old surviving victim of the Zodiac killer. He was picked up by Darlene Ferrin on the night of the attack, an event that became a significant part of the Zodiac killer's crime spree. Mageau notably saw the killer without a mask during the incident, providing a crucial eyewitness account. Despite this direct encounter, he never made a positive identification of the perpetrator. His testimony was an integral part of the Vallejo investigation into the Zodiac killings, and he was later contacted by Sergeant Bawart for a photo array as part of ongoing efforts to identify the killer. Mageau's harrowing experience has also been depicted as a character in scripts related to the Zodiac case.

[VALLEJO, CALIFORNIA]
Description: A small town in California where the initial events of the script take place.

[SEPTEMBER 27, 1969 KILLING]
Description: The killing on September 27, 1969, at 6:30 PM, is the attack on Bryan and Cecelia at Lake Berryessa, attributed to Zodiac, and mentioned on Bryan's car.

[CECELIA]
Description: Cecelia was involved in a traumatic incident at Lake Berryessa. While in a public park area with Bryan, she was accosted by an individual referred to as "The Man." During this encounter, Cecelia was robbed and tied up, and was also forced to tie Bryan. The incident tragically culminated in Cecelia becoming a victim of a fatal stabbing attack.

[BRYAN]
Description: Bryan, a sociology major, was the victim of a stabbing attack. Accounts of the incident describe him as being in a public park with Cecelia, where he was robbed, tied up, and stabbed by an assailant referred to as The Man. Another description places the stabbing attack at Lake Berryessa. Despite the assault, Bryan survived the attack, successfully freeing himself and calling for help.

[TOSCHI]
Description: **TOSCHI** is a prominent and deeply invested detective and inspector, primarily affiliated with the Homicide Unit of the San Francisco Police Department (SFPD) at the Hall of Justice. He is widely recognized as the lead investigator in the complex and frustrating Zodiac Killer case.

Throughout his extensive involvement, Toschi worked closely with partners such as Armstrong, Mulanax, Narlow, and Nicolai, and briefed superiors like Captain Lee and Captain Cross. He was instrumental in leading the police investigation, actively pursuing leads, and coordinating with various law enforcement personnel. His duties included leading the search of Arthur Leigh Allen's residence, interviewing suspects like Allen, and reviewing evidence, including Robert Graysmith's findings linking Allen to the Zodiac.

Toschi received direct communications from the Zodiac Killer and even a letter from Leigh Allen. He was closely involved with the Office of Questioned Documents, consulting with experts like Terry Pascoe on handwriting analysis, though he often expressed impatience with the pace of their work. He regularly visited the scene of Paul Stine's murder at Washington and Cherry, sitting vigil and interviewing patrolmen Fouke and Zelms.

His dedication to the case was evident in his frustration with the lack of progress, the public's fear, and the press. He led meetings with bus drivers, monitored television broadcasts, and coordinated responses to the Zodiac's calls. Toschi was also the focus of Melvin Belli's attention during a broadcast and escorted Belli to KGO Television. He was mentioned in a Zodiac letter himself, leading to an approach by Internal Affairs for a handwriting sample.

Toschi was a key consultant for Robert Graysmith, initially reluctant but eventually providing crucial leads and advice. He discussed theories and evidence with Graysmith, expressing his strong belief that Arthur Leigh Allen was the killer. Graysmith often echoed Toschi's observations and even woke him in the middle of the night with new discoveries. Toschi also investigated the Cheri Jo Bates murder for its potential Zodiac connection and examined Zodiac letters and bomb diagrams, suggesting military consultation.

Despite the immense pressure and the case's toll, Toschi remained deeply committed, though at one point he was implied to be trying to distance himself from the case, perhaps due to burnout or its unresolved nature. He is an experienced murder police officer whose work on the Zodiac case made him a central figure in the investigation.

[ARTHUR LEIGH ALLEN]
Description: Arthur Leigh Allen, born December 18, 1933, was the primary suspect in the Zodiac Killer case, identified by Graysmith as the perpetrator in his investigation and by "Mike" as his shooter. He was widely believed to be the "Zodiac" killer.

Allen had a background as a Navy man and worked as a chemist, including at Union Oil in Pinole. He was also a former public school teacher, specifically at Valley Springs, but was fired from elementary schools for molesting children or touching kids. Notably, he was fired eight months before the first Vallejo murder. He was later arrested for molestation in January 1975.

Regarding his connection to the Zodiac case, Allen was interrogated by Inspectors Armstrong, Toschi, and Sergeant Mulanax, and his investigation was reopened by Sergeant Bawart. He denied involvement in the murders and provided explanations for incriminating statements and items. He was interviewed by Toschi on August 4, 1971, and also wrote a letter to Toschi. Allegations against him included discussing hunting people and using the name "Zodiac" in 1968.

Investigators conducted searches of his residence and basement (in 1991), and he was brought to the Hall of Justice for investigation. He was known to drive a white Kharmann Ghia. While he was noted to live in Vallejo at some point, his trailer was moved to Santa Rosa on August 7, 1971, indicating a later residence there.

Allen was described as being sick with diabetes and possibly ambidextrous. He died of a heart attack in 1992 before he could be arrested for the murders. DNA tests conducted on Zodiac envelopes did not match his DNA.

[VALLEJO MURDERS]
Description: A series of murders that occurred in Vallejo, a city where Arthur Leigh Allen resides and for which he lacked an alibi.

=== ENTITIES ===

[MAGEAU]
Description: Mageau is an individual connected to the Zodiac investigation, specifically the Vallejo case. He was a victim who survived a Zodiac attack. Investigator Graysmith is actively trying to locate Mageau as part of his ongoing investigation, believing that Mageau might have known the Zodiac killer. However, Mageau is currently described as "gone" and cannot be found.

[FERRIN]
Description: A victim of the Zodiac who died in an attack.

[ZODIAC]
Description: "ZODIAC" refers to the notorious and unidentified serial killer whose identity, crimes, letters, and patterns are the central focus of extensive investigations. This "very bad man" and criminal is responsible for a series of unsolved murders, including a believed 1966 Southern California murder. The killer adopted the moniker "Zodiac" and is associated with a distinctive crosshair symbol.

The Zodiac Killer communicated through calls and letters, with handwriting from these letters being a key piece of evidence. The activities, claims, and potential true identity of Zodiac have been the subject of ongoing police and journalistic investigations, notably by Sergeant Bawart and Detective Toschi in the past.

Robert Graysmith became obsessed with the case, investigating it extensively and eventually writing a book titled "Zodiac," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. Graysmith even sketched a costume for Zodiac, inspired by Count Zaroff.

Arthur Leigh Allen is a prominent suspect in the case, having allegedly planned to use the name "Zodiac" to communicate with the police. He was also noted to have worn the Zodiac crosshair symbol on his watch and mentioned the name a year and a half before it appeared in any of the killer's letters. Another individual, Sam, is implied to be the Zodiac caller. Despite these leads and suspects, the true identity of the Zodiac Killer remains unknown.

=== ENTITIES ===

[ZODIAC]
Description: "ZODIAC" refers to the notorious and unidentified serial killer whose identity, crimes, letters, and patterns are the central focus of extensive investigations. This "very bad man" and criminal is responsible for a series of unsolved murders, including a believed 1966 Southern California murder. The killer adopted the moniker "Zodiac" and is associated with a distinctive crosshair symbol.

The Zodiac Killer communicated through calls and letters, with handwriting from these letters being a key piece of evidence. The activities, claims, and potential true identity of Zodiac have been the subject of ongoing police and journalistic investigations, notably by Sergeant Bawart and Detective Toschi in the past.

Robert Graysmith became obsessed with the case, investigating it extensively and eventually writing a book titled "Zodiac," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. Graysmith even sketched a costume for Zodiac, inspired by Count Zaroff.

Arthur Leigh Allen is a prominent suspect in the case, having allegedly planned to use the name "Zodiac" to communicate with the police. He was also noted to have worn the Zodiac crosshair symbol on his watch and mentioned the name a year and a half before it appeared in any of the killer's letters. Another individual, Sam, is implied to be the Zodiac caller. Despite these leads and suspects, the true identity of the Zodiac Killer remains unknown.

[DARLENE FERRIN]
Description: Darlene Ferrin was a 22-year-old woman who tragically became a victim of the Zodiac killer. On July 4th, she was driving and picked up Mike Mageau, shortly before she was shot and murdered at Blue Rock Springs. She did not survive the attack. Her case is a significant part of the Vallejo investigation into the Zodiac killer, and her murder and connections are also being investigated by Graysmith and Toschi. Florence Douglas mentioned Darlene Ferrin's case, suggesting that crucial clues might have been overlooked. Darlene Ferrin reportedly knew a man named "Lee," who is suspected to be Leigh Allen. Prior to her death, she was reportedly scared of an unknown man she had encountered at a painting party, and she was followed before the fatal shooting.

[JULY 4TH]
Description: The date of a shooting involving Darlene Ferrin and Michael Mayhew.

question: Who identifies Allen as the killer to the police?
response: Don Cheney identifies Arthur Leigh Allen as the killer to the police. He recounts a conversation with Allen on New Year's Day, 1968, where Allen discussed hunting people, using a light on a gun as a sight, and calling himself "Zodiac" to mess with the police. Cheney also mentioned Allen's anger about losing his teaching job and his threats to shoot out the tires of a school bus and pick off "little darlings." Cheney initially tried to report this to local police but was dismissed, and later his friend Sandy Panzarella helped him contact the Manhattan Beach P.D. [Data: Don Cheney, Arthur Leigh Allen]

=== ENTITIES ===

[ARTHUR LEIGH ALLEN]
Description: Arthur Leigh Allen, born December 18, 1933, was the primary suspect in the Zodiac Killer case, identified by Graysmith as the perpetrator in his investigation and by "Mike" as his shooter. He was widely believed to be the "Zodiac" killer.

Allen had a background as a Navy man and worked as a chemist, including at Union Oil in Pinole. He was also a former public school teacher, specifically at Valley Springs, but was fired from elementary schools for molesting children or touching kids. Notably, he was fired eight months before the first Vallejo murder. He was later arrested for molestation in January 1975.

Regarding his connection to the Zodiac case, Allen was interrogated by Inspectors Armstrong, Toschi, and Sergeant Mulanax, and his investigation was reopened by Sergeant Bawart. He denied involvement in the murders and provided explanations for incriminating statements and items. He was interviewed by Toschi on August 4, 1971, and also wrote a letter to Toschi. Allegations against him included discussing hunting people and using the name "Zodiac" in 1968.

Investigators conducted searches of his residence and basement (in 1991), and he was brought to the Hall of Justice for investigation. He was known to drive a white Kharmann Ghia. While he was noted to live in Vallejo at some point, his trailer was moved to Santa Rosa on August 7, 1971, indicating a later residence there.

Allen was described as being sick with diabetes and possibly ambidextrous. He died of a heart attack in 1992 before he could be arrested for the murders. DNA tests conducted on Zodiac envelopes did not match his DNA.

[STINE'S KEYS]
Description: An item belonging to Stine that was not found in Allen's trailer.

[ROBERT GRAYSMITH]
Description: Robert Graysmith was a cartoonist at the San Francisco Chronicle who developed a profound interest in the Zodiac killer's codes and letters, dedicating himself to deciphering them. Living in San Francisco, he was in his mid-20s, a father to David, and Melanie's partner, residing in a cluttered apartment. He reacted negatively to news about a rapist and later stopped receiving anonymous phone calls after Arthur Leigh Allen's death.

Graysmith's deep fascination with the Zodiac case led him to collect newspaper clippings and conduct extensive personal research into the killer's codes. He expressed his interest in the case to Dave Toschi and visited Paul Avery to discuss the possibility of writing a book about it. He also met with Vaughn to discuss a film and a film canister pertinent to his investigation.

His dedicated work as a civilian investigator culminated in him authoring the books "Zodiac" and "Zodiac Unmasked," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. His investigations and writings were instrumental in leading to the reopening of the Zodiac case, with a focus on Arthur Leigh Allen. Despite his significant contributions to the case, his conclusions on the Zodiac case are believed by many to be incorrect.

[ARTHUR LEIGH ALLEN'S DEATH]
Description: No description available

[CATHERINE ALLEN]
Description: Catherine Allen is identified as the sister-in-law of Arthur Leigh Allen, a primary suspect in the Zodiac investigation, and the wife of John Allen. She has been actively involved in the case, having been interviewed by Detective Armstrong and assisting detectives by searching for a Christmas card and providing information about Leigh Allen. Catherine Allen also inquired about the status of the case. Notably, she believes that Leigh Allen might be the Zodiac suspect. She provided specific information, stating that Arthur Leigh Allen cleaned out his trailer and moved it to Santa Rosa on August 7, 1971. Furthermore, Catherine Allen identified a unique spelling in a Zodiac letter, contributing another piece of potential evidence to the investigation.

[JOHN ALLEN]
Description: Leigh Allen's brother, interviewed by detectives, and husband of Catherine Allen.

=== ENTITIES ===

[ARTHUR LEIGH ALLEN]
Description: Arthur Leigh Allen, born December 18, 1933, was the primary suspect in the Zodiac Killer case, identified by Graysmith as the perpetrator in his investigation and by "Mike" as his shooter. He was widely believed to be the "Zodiac" killer.

Allen had a background as a Navy man and worked as a chemist, including at Union Oil in Pinole. He was also a former public school teacher, specifically at Valley Springs, but was fired from elementary schools for molesting children or touching kids. Notably, he was fired eight months before the first Vallejo murder. He was later arrested for molestation in January 1975.

Regarding his connection to the Zodiac case, Allen was interrogated by Inspectors Armstrong, Toschi, and Sergeant Mulanax, and his investigation was reopened by Sergeant Bawart. He denied involvement in the murders and provided explanations for incriminating statements and items. He was interviewed by Toschi on August 4, 1971, and also wrote a letter to Toschi. Allegations against him included discussing hunting people and using the name "Zodiac" in 1968.

Investigators conducted searches of his residence and basement (in 1991), and he was brought to the Hall of Justice for investigation. He was known to drive a white Kharmann Ghia. While he was noted to live in Vallejo at some point, his trailer was moved to Santa Rosa on August 7, 1971, indicating a later residence there.

Allen was described as being sick with diabetes and possibly ambidextrous. He died of a heart attack in 1992 before he could be arrested for the murders. DNA tests conducted on Zodiac envelopes did not match his DNA.

[ARTHUR LEIGH ALLEN'S DEATH]
Description: No description available

[DON CHENEY]
Description: Don Cheney is a key individual who played a significant role in the Zodiac killer investigation, primarily by implicating Arthur Leigh Allen. He was Arthur Leigh Allen's former roommate and contacted the police regarding him.

On New Year's Day, 1968, Cheney had a conversation with Arthur Leigh Allen where Allen discussed plans related to the Zodiac killer. Allen also reportedly told Cheney about hunting people and referred to himself as "Zodiac." Cheney later tried to report this information to the police.

Cheney provided a sworn statement detailing these revelations, becoming the man who first implicated Arthur Leigh Allen as the Zodiac killer. He subsequently passed a polygraph test, which was crucial in securing a warrant for a basement search as part of the investigation. Additionally, Don Cheney met with Armstrong and Sandy Panzarella at the Science Dynamics Building on July 26, 1971.

[LA]
Description: Los Angeles, where Don Cheney started a new job on January 20th, 1968, a detail used to confirm the timeline of his conversation with Allen.

[ROBERT GRAYSMITH]
Description: Robert Graysmith was a cartoonist at the San Francisco Chronicle who developed a profound interest in the Zodiac killer's codes and letters, dedicating himself to deciphering them. Living in San Francisco, he was in his mid-20s, a father to David, and Melanie's partner, residing in a cluttered apartment. He reacted negatively to news about a rapist and later stopped receiving anonymous phone calls after Arthur Leigh Allen's death.

Graysmith's deep fascination with the Zodiac case led him to collect newspaper clippings and conduct extensive personal research into the killer's codes. He expressed his interest in the case to Dave Toschi and visited Paul Avery to discuss the possibility of writing a book about it. He also met with Vaughn to discuss a film and a film canister pertinent to his investigation.

His dedicated work as a civilian investigator culminated in him authoring the books "Zodiac" and "Zodiac Unmasked," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. His investigations and writings were instrumental in leading to the reopening of the Zodiac case, with a focus on Arthur Leigh Allen. Despite his significant contributions to the case, his conclusions on the Zodiac case are believed by many to be incorrect.

=== ENTITIES ===

[SEPTEMBER 27, 1969 KILLING]
Description: The killing on September 27, 1969, at 6:30 PM, is the attack on Bryan and Cecelia at Lake Berryessa, attributed to Zodiac, and mentioned on Bryan's car.

[CECELIA]
Description: Cecelia was involved in a traumatic incident at Lake Berryessa. While in a public park area with Bryan, she was accosted by an individual referred to as "The Man." During this encounter, Cecelia was robbed and tied up, and was also forced to tie Bryan. The incident tragically culminated in Cecelia becoming a victim of a fatal stabbing attack.

[THE MAN]
Description: "THE MAN" is an unnamed assailant, later identified as Zodiac, responsible for a series of violent crimes. During one attack, he was described as wearing a distinctive outfit that included a hood resembling an executioner's mask, sunglasses, and a cross stitched into his hood. He was armed with both a sheathed knife and a gun.

Among his known actions, "THE MAN" robbed Bryan and Cecelia at Lake Berryessa, where he tied them up and stabbed Bryan. He also sabotaged Kathleen Johns' car, subsequently offering her a lift before threatening to kill her and her baby. In another incident, "THE MAN," initially disguised as a police officer, shot and murdered Mike and Darlene. Following this double murder, he called the police himself to report the crime, claiming responsibility for killing "those kids last year," implying previous victims. During one encounter, he made claims of having killed a guard while escaping from prison in Montana and expressed intentions to travel to Mexico.

[BRYAN]
Description: Bryan, a sociology major, was the victim of a stabbing attack. Accounts of the incident describe him as being in a public park with Cecelia, where he was robbed, tied up, and stabbed by an assailant referred to as The Man. Another description places the stabbing attack at Lake Berryessa. Despite the assault, Bryan survived the attack, successfully freeing himself and calling for help.


=== RELATIONSHIPS ===

- CECELIA --[Cecelia was a victim of the fatal stabbing attack on September 27, 1969.]--> SEPTEMBER 27, 1969 KILLING

- BRYAN --[The Man robbed Bryan, forced Cecelia to tie him, and ultimately stabbed him. This violent encounter, where The Man stabbed Bryan multiple times, took place at Lake Berryessa.]--> THE MAN

- BRYAN --[Bryan and Cecelia were together when they became victims of a violent incident. This event occurred at Lake Berryessa, which can be characterized as a public recreational area. During the incident, they were subjected to a stabbing attack, which was part of a broader assault. They were also victims of robbery. The perpetrator of these acts was identified as "The Man."]--> CECELIA

=== ENTITIES ===

[ZODIAC]
Description: "ZODIAC" refers to the notorious and unidentified serial killer whose identity, crimes, letters, and patterns are the central focus of extensive investigations. This "very bad man" and criminal is responsible for a series of unsolved murders, including a believed 1966 Southern California murder. The killer adopted the moniker "Zodiac" and is associated with a distinctive crosshair symbol.

The Zodiac Killer communicated through calls and letters, with handwriting from these letters being a key piece of evidence. The activities, claims, and potential true identity of Zodiac have been the subject of ongoing police and journalistic investigations, notably by Sergeant Bawart and Detective Toschi in the past.

Robert Graysmith became obsessed with the case, investigating it extensively and eventually writing a book titled "Zodiac," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. Graysmith even sketched a costume for Zodiac, inspired by Count Zaroff.

Arthur Leigh Allen is a prominent suspect in the case, having allegedly planned to use the name "Zodiac" to communicate with the police. He was also noted to have worn the Zodiac crosshair symbol on his watch and mentioned the name a year and a half before it appeared in any of the killer's letters. Another individual, Sam, is implied to be the Zodiac caller. Despite these leads and suspects, the true identity of the Zodiac Killer remains unknown.

[LETTERS]
Description: Communications written by the Zodiac killer.

[VALLEJO TIMES]
Description: A newspaper that also received a part of the murderer's cipher.

[CIPHER]
Description: A coded message included in the murderer's letter, claimed to contain the murderer's identity, with parts sent to different newspapers for publication.

[S.F. EXAMINER]
Description: A newspaper in the Bay Area that also received a part of the murderer's cipher.

=== ENTITIES ===

[PAUL AVERY]
Description: Paul Avery is a journalist, described as a "great reporter" and a well-dressed crime reporter. He initially worked on the third floor of the San Francisco Chronicle, where he was a colleague of Robert Graysmith. During his tenure at the Chronicle, Avery wrote numerous articles about the Zodiac case, provided information, and discussed the killer's activities and messages with Graysmith. He was directly threatened by the Zodiac killer and attempted to interview Inspector Toschi, whom Graysmith believed Avery might know.

Later in his career, Paul Avery moved to the Sacramento Bee, where he lived on a houseboat. By this point, his perspective on the Zodiac case had shifted; he became dismissive of its importance, focusing instead on selling newspapers, and reacted with cynicism to news of Graysmith's success in decoding the Zodiac's cipher. Despite this change, Graysmith still sought him out to discuss writing a book about Zodiac. Avery was also known to follow leads, such as one in Riverside to meet an anonymous tipster, for which he carried a gun. His drinking habits were significant enough to be used by Graysmith as a comparison for another individual.

[ROBERT GRAYSMITH]
Description: Robert Graysmith was a cartoonist at the San Francisco Chronicle who developed a profound interest in the Zodiac killer's codes and letters, dedicating himself to deciphering them. Living in San Francisco, he was in his mid-20s, a father to David, and Melanie's partner, residing in a cluttered apartment. He reacted negatively to news about a rapist and later stopped receiving anonymous phone calls after Arthur Leigh Allen's death.

Graysmith's deep fascination with the Zodiac case led him to collect newspaper clippings and conduct extensive personal research into the killer's codes. He expressed his interest in the case to Dave Toschi and visited Paul Avery to discuss the possibility of writing a book about it. He also met with Vaughn to discuss a film and a film canister pertinent to his investigation.

His dedicated work as a civilian investigator culminated in him authoring the books "Zodiac" and "Zodiac Unmasked," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. His investigations and writings were instrumental in leading to the reopening of the Zodiac case, with a focus on Arthur Leigh Allen. Despite his significant contributions to the case, his conclusions on the Zodiac case are believed by many to be incorrect.

[SAN FRANCISCO CHRONICLE]
Description: The SAN FRANCISCO CHRONICLE is a major, grand old newspaper building located on Fifth and Mission in San Francisco, often referred to informally as "the Chron" or "the Chronicle."

The newspaper serves as a workplace for a significant number of reporters, columnists, and staff members, many of whom are central to the investigation of the Zodiac killer. Notable employees include Paul Avery, a reporter and columnist who extensively covers the Zodiac case, attempts to influence the investigation, and monitors related broadcasts; Robert Graysmith, a cartoonist and reporter who works on the third floor, investigates the Zodiac killings, and uses the newspaper as a base for his inquiries; Duffy Jennings, who now works there; columnists Herb Caen and Armistead Maupin; and other staff members such as Shorty, Carol Fisher, Templeton Peck, Charles De Young Theriot, and Hyman. Detectives Toschi and Armstrong are also noted to visit the newspaper office.

The SAN FRANCISCO CHRONICLE plays a pivotal role in the Zodiac killer case, as it is the primary recipient of letters, ciphers, and coded messages from the killer, including those claiming responsibility for murders. The newspaper faces critical decisions regarding whether to publish these communications, often engaging in internal debates about their content and potential impact. It cooperates with the San Francisco Police Department (SFPD) on publishing Zodiac letters and has published various articles related to the killer, including a front-page story about a police officer shooting. Its journalists actively investigate the Zodiac killings, using the newspaper office as a hub for their efforts and monitoring live television broadcasts related to the case.

[PRESCHOOL]
Description: The educational institution where David, Robert Graysmith's son, attends.

=== ENTITIES ===

[SEPTEMBER 27, 1969]
Description: The date when Bryan Hartnell and Cecelia Shephard were attacked by the Zodiac killer at Lake Berryessa.

[CECELIA SHEPHARD]
Description: A college student who, along with Bryan Hartnell, was attacked by the Zodiac killer at Lake Berryessa.

[LAKE BERRYESSA]
Description: Lake Berryessa is a geographical location and a public park situated in Napa County, California. It is notably recognized as one of the Zodiac Killer's attack sites. At this location, college students Bryan Hartnell and Cecelia Shephard were attacked, specifically stabbed, by the individual known as "The Man" or the Zodiac Killer. During investigations at Lake Berryessa, a suspect resembling Arthur Leigh Allen was reportedly seen, and military bootprints were discovered.

[BRYAN HARTNELL]
Description: Bryan Hartnell was a college student who, along with Cecelia Shephard, was attacked by the Zodiac killer at Lake Berryessa. He survived the brutal assault, sustaining wounds during the incident. Following the attack, Bryan Hartnell listened to a tape of a caller's voice, believed to be the Zodiac's, but identified it as "not him," noting that the voice was too high and too young compared to the attacker's voice he remembered. Additionally, Bryan Hartnell owned a white Kharmann Ghia, a detail that drew attention because his car was identical to one owned by Arthur Leigh Allen, a person of interest in the Zodiac case, implying a potential connection to the broader investigation or his status as a victim.

=== ENTITIES ===

[ZODIAC]
Description: "ZODIAC" refers to the notorious and unidentified serial killer whose identity, crimes, letters, and patterns are the central focus of extensive investigations. This "very bad man" and criminal is responsible for a series of unsolved murders, including a believed 1966 Southern California murder. The killer adopted the moniker "Zodiac" and is associated with a distinctive crosshair symbol.

The Zodiac Killer communicated through calls and letters, with handwriting from these letters being a key piece of evidence. The activities, claims, and potential true identity of Zodiac have been the subject of ongoing police and journalistic investigations, notably by Sergeant Bawart and Detective Toschi in the past.

Robert Graysmith became obsessed with the case, investigating it extensively and eventually writing a book titled "Zodiac," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. Graysmith even sketched a costume for Zodiac, inspired by Count Zaroff.

Arthur Leigh Allen is a prominent suspect in the case, having allegedly planned to use the name "Zodiac" to communicate with the police. He was also noted to have worn the Zodiac crosshair symbol on his watch and mentioned the name a year and a half before it appeared in any of the killer's letters. Another individual, Sam, is implied to be the Zodiac caller. Despite these leads and suspects, the true identity of the Zodiac Killer remains unknown.

[CIPHER SLAYER]
Description: An alias for the Zodiac killer.

[CIPHER]
Description: A coded message included in the murderer's letter, claimed to contain the murderer's identity, with parts sent to different newspapers for publication.

[KILL RAMPAGE THREAT]
Description: The murderer's explicit threat to commit a series of killings if the cipher is not published by a specific date.

Description: The specific date when the events in the script begin, coinciding with the Summer of Love.

[PAINTING PARTY]
Description: The "PAINTING PARTY" was a social gathering hosted by Darlene Ferrin and her husband at their new house, where guests helped with painting. During the event, a mysterious man, who was not George Waters, appeared and scared Darlene. This gathering, which involved Darlene, was later reported to the police by Linda Del Buono and is currently a subject of inquiry for Graysmith.

[VALLEJO, CALIFORNIA]
Description: A small town in California where the initial events of the script take place.

[DARLENE FERRIN]
Description: Darlene Ferrin was a 22-year-old woman who tragically became a victim of the Zodiac killer. On July 4th, she was driving and picked up Mike Mageau, shortly before she was shot and murdered at Blue Rock Springs. She did not survive the attack. Her case is a significant part of the Vallejo investigation into the Zodiac killer, and her murder and connections are also being investigated by Graysmith and Toschi. Florence Douglas mentioned Darlene Ferrin's case, suggesting that crucial clues might have been overlooked. Darlene Ferrin reportedly knew a man named "Lee," who is suspected to be Leigh Allen. Prior to her death, she was reportedly scared of an unknown man she had encountered at a painting party, and she was followed before the fatal shooting.

[MIKE MAGEAU]
Description: Mike Mageau was a 19-year-old surviving victim of the Zodiac killer. He was picked up by Darlene Ferrin on the night of the attack, an event that became a significant part of the Zodiac killer's crime spree. Mageau notably saw the killer without a mask during the incident, providing a crucial eyewitness account. Despite this direct encounter, he never made a positive identification of the perpetrator. His testimony was an integral part of the Vallejo investigation into the Zodiac killings, and he was later contacted by Sergeant Bawart for a photo array as part of ongoing efforts to identify the killer. Mageau's harrowing experience has also been depicted as a character in scripts related to the Zodiac case.

[ZODIAC]
Description: "ZODIAC" refers to the notorious and unidentified serial killer whose identity, crimes, letters, and patterns are the central focus of extensive investigations. This "very bad man" and criminal is responsible for a series of unsolved murders, including a believed 1966 Southern California murder. The killer adopted the moniker "Zodiac" and is associated with a distinctive crosshair symbol.

The Zodiac Killer communicated through calls and letters, with handwriting from these letters being a key piece of evidence. The activities, claims, and potential true identity of Zodiac have been the subject of ongoing police and journalistic investigations, notably by Sergeant Bawart and Detective Toschi in the past.

Robert Graysmith became obsessed with the case, investigating it extensively and eventually writing a book titled "Zodiac," which the script "Chronicles" is based upon. Graysmith even sketched a costume for Zodiac, inspired by Count Zaroff.

Arthur Leigh Allen is a prominent suspect in the case, having allegedly planned to use the name "Zodiac" to communicate with the police. He was also noted to have worn the Zodiac crosshair symbol on his watch and mentioned the name a year and a half before it appeared in any of the killer's letters. Another individual, Sam, is implied to be the Zodiac caller. Despite these leads and suspects, the true identity of the Zodiac Killer remains unknown.

=== ENTITIES ===

[LEE]
Description: A mysterious man, also referred to as Leigh, who attended Darlene's "painting party," brought her presents from Tia Juana (Tijuana, Mexico), and Darlene was scared of him. Linda believes he might have killed someone, possibly while in the service."

[TIA JUANA]
Description: A location, likely Tijuana, Mexico, from which Lee brought presents to Darlene."

[MEXICO]
Description: Mexico is a country that features in two distinct narrative threads. It is identified as the origin point from which a mysterious man, referred to as Lee or Leigh, brought presents to Darlene. Additionally, Mexico is the planned destination for "The Man" after he commits a robbery against Bryan and Cecelia.

[MIKE MAGEAU]
Description: Mike Mageau was a 19-year-old surviving victim of the Zodiac killer. He was picked up by Darlene Ferrin on the night of the attack, an event that became a significant part of the Zodiac killer's crime spree. Mageau notably saw the killer without a mask during the incident, providing a crucial eyewitness account. Despite this direct encounter, he never made a positive identification of the perpetrator. His testimony was an integral part of the Vallejo investigation into the Zodiac killings, and he was later contacted by Sergeant Bawart for a photo array as part of ongoing efforts to identify the killer. Mageau's harrowing experience has also been depicted as a character in scripts related to the Zodiac case.

[VALLEJO, CALIFORNIA]
Description: A small town in California where the initial events of the script take place.

[MR. ED'S]
Description: A local teen hangout location in Vallejo where Darlene and Mike briefly cruise through.

question: What happens to Mike and Darlene when after they are attacked?
response: After Mike and Darlene are attacked by "THE MAN" [Data: Entities (THE MAN)], they are shot multiple times. Mike is shot in the face, neck, and arm, with some bullets passing through him into Darlene. Darlene is shot twice in each arm and three times in the back. "THE MAN" then fires two more shots into Mike, propelling him into the back seat, and two more into Darlene before leaving. Later, police arrive to find Mike slumped against the rear of the Corvair and Darlene in even worse condition in the front seat. Mike is able to report a double murder and identify the killer as having also killed "those kids last year."

=== ENTITIES ===

[JULY 4TH, 1969]
Description: The specific date when the events in the script begin, coinciding with the Summer of Love.

[MR. ED'S]
Description: A local teen hangout location in Vallejo where Darlene and Mike briefly cruise through.

[THE MAN]
Description: "THE MAN" is an unnamed assailant, later identified as Zodiac, responsible for a series of violent crimes. During one attack, he was described as wearing a distinctive outfit that included a hood resembling an executioner's mask, sunglasses, and a cross stitched into his hood. He was armed with both a sheathed knife and a gun.

Among his known actions, "THE MAN" robbed Bryan and Cecelia at Lake Berryessa, where he tied them up and stabbed Bryan. He also sabotaged Kathleen Johns' car, subsequently offering her a lift before threatening to kill her and her baby. In another incident, "THE MAN," initially disguised as a police officer, shot and murdered Mike and Darlene. Following this double murder, he called the police himself to report the crime, claiming responsibility for killing "those kids last year," implying previous victims. During one encounter, he made claims of having killed a guard while escaping from prison in Montana and expressed intentions to travel to Mexico.

[DARLENE]
Description: Darlene was an individual known by Linda Del Buono, who described her as someone who "always had lots of boys around" and was married. Darlene hosted or was involved in a "painting party" where a "weird" guy was present. Linda also noted that Darlene was scared of a particular man named Lee/Leigh. Darlene was tragically murdered, having been shot multiple times in a Corvair in the Blue Rock Springs parking lot alongside a person named Mike. Her death is considered relevant to the Zodiac investigation, with Graysmith having contacted her family in an attempt to find her and believing she was possibly connected to the case. Graysmith also believes that Rick Marshall knew Darlene.

[LEE]
Description: A mysterious man, also referred to as Leigh, who attended Darlene's "painting party," brought her presents from Tia Juana (Tijuana, Mexico), and Darlene was scared of him. Linda believes he might have killed someone, possibly while in the service."

[MEXICO]
Description: Mexico is a country that features in two distinct narrative threads. It is identified as the origin point from which a mysterious man, referred to as Lee or Leigh, brought presents to Darlene. Additionally, Mexico is the planned destination for "The Man" after he commits a robbery against Bryan and Cecelia.
